stories.title: Typhoons batter East Asia as El Niño makes Pacific 'burn with fever'
summary: Even for countries where typhoons are a way of life, the last few months have brought unusually wild weather.

stories.title: Scientists may have finally explained why our brains and bodies are cross-wired
summary: Scientists propose that the brain’s mysterious cross-wiring, which connects each hemisphere to the opposite side of the body, may have originated more than 500 million years ago in the visual systems of ancient fish.
Rather than evolving for a specific advantage, this unusual arrangement may simply be a legacy of evolution building new brain circuits on an ancient foundation.

stories.title: Permanent daylight saving time has a dark side, scientists warn
summary: A new study warns that permanent daylight saving time could force American children to make at least 2 billion additional school commutes in darkness, potentially increasing safety risks and disrupting their biological clocks.
Researchers found that fatal crashes involving school-aged pedestrians were roughly twice as likely during dark mornings as after sunrise.

stories.title: A tiny squeeze dramatically changes the magnetism of exotic materials
summary: Scientists have discovered that a simple mechanical squeeze can dramatically alter the magnetic properties and electrical behavior of exotic materials called altermagnets.
The surprising breakthrough could open the door to faster, more energy-efficient electronics and new technologies for quantum computing.

stories.title: MIT scientists break a 20-year rule and unlock never-before-seen crystal structures
summary: MIT scientists have challenged two decades of conventional thinking by discovering that flexible molecular connections, rather than rigid ones, can unlock entirely new ways to arrange nanoparticles.
The breakthrough could lead to a new generation of designer materials with unusual properties and applications in electronics, medicine, and energy.

stories.title: William meets firefighters who tackled summer blazes
summary: The prince says 2026 was the first summer he felt "worried about the scale of the wildfires".

stories.title: NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope
summary: NASA is exploring a daring plan to save the legendary Hubble Space Telescope from its eventual fiery plunge into Earth's atmosphere.
After more than 35 years of groundbreaking discoveries, Hubble is slowly losing altitude, and without intervention, it could fall back to Earth as early as 2033 or 2034.

To keep the iconic observatory operating, NASA is asking private space companies to propose innovative ways to boost Hubble into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission finally ends.

stories.title: SLAC scientists find conclusive proof of a mysterious third type of magnetism
summary: For nearly 90 years, scientists believed magnetism fell into just two categories, but researchers have now confirmed a remarkable third type called altermagnetism.
Using specialized X-rays, they uncovered a unique magnetic signature that proves these materials behave differently from conventional magnets.
Altermagnets combine stability with the ability to efficiently carry information, potentially overcoming major limitations in today's electronics.

stories.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage
summary: Stanford researchers have discovered an AI-identified natural molecule that dramatically suppresses appetite and promotes fat loss in animals, potentially offering an Ozempic-like weight-loss treatment without common digestive side effects or significant muscle loss.
Called BRP, the molecule reduced food intake by up to 50% and targets a different brain pathway, raising hopes for a more precise obesity treatment if future human trials prove successful.

stories.title: Tiktoker 'super excited' to co-host BBC nature show
summary: Naturewatch, hosted by Chris Packham, Megan McCubbin and Kyle Thomas, is being made in Bristol.

stories.title: Prince William says UK faces terrifying risk of more wildfires due to climate change
summary: The prince says 2026 was the first summer he felt "worried about the scale of the wildfires".

stories.title: Trust vows to 'maintain spirit' of nature reserve
summary: Flatford Wildlife Garden is bought by the National Trust after being run by the RSPB for 15 years.

stories.title: Gene editing could replace a lifetime of medication, but there's a catch
summary: A single gene-editing treatment could someday protect against heart disease, high cholesterol, and other common conditions for decades, potentially replacing lifelong medications.
But scientists warn that permanently altering genes introduces risks that could take years to emerge, making long-term safety a critical challenge.

stories.title: Scientists trick cancer cells into making the drugs that kill them
summary: Scientists have developed a promising new cancer-fighting strategy that uses carbon monoxide naturally produced by tumor cells to manufacture powerful drugs inside the cancer cells themselves.
Early laboratory experiments suggest the technique could selectively attack cancer while sparing healthy cells, potentially paving the way for safer chemotherapy alternatives.

stories.title: A hidden star is plowing through Betelgeuse’s atmosphere, new evidence suggests
summary: Something mysterious is disturbing Betelgeuse, and astronomers believe they have identified the culprit: a hidden companion star called Siwarha.
New radio observations reveal that the smaller star may be plowing through Betelgeuse’s enormous atmosphere, creating disturbances that subtly stretch and distort the red supergiant’s shape.

stories.title: Kids who eat more ultra-processed foods show a troubling brain response
summary: A new study suggests that ultra-processed foods may influence children's developing brains in ways that encourage weight gain.

Researchers from USC studied 46 children ages 7 to 10 and found that those who ate more ultra-processed foods showed stronger activity in the brain's reward system when viewing tempting foods like cookies and French fries.

These heightened brain responses were linked to greater increases in body fat and body mass index (BMI) one year later, suggesting that the brain's sensitivity to food cues may help explain why ultra-processed diets are associated with obesity.

stories.title: Action needed to tackle 'biodiversity crisis'
summary: The issue is part of wider concerns the government is not focused enough on the environment.
